raw_response:
The bug is in silver_transactions: txn_date is derived from ingest_ts, which is the batch delivery time and is always the day after the transaction. The alert says 4600 rows differ, which is every POSTED row. The sample shows txn_ts on the 15th with ingest_ts on the 16th. The change note from 2026-01-16 (DE-398, refactored date derivation) points to the same cause.

The correct rule is almost certainly txn_date = CAST(txn_ts AS DATE). The monitor itself defines consistency as txn_date matching the date of txn_ts. Every batch contains transactions from a single day, so the ingest-based date is just a uniform shift of one day.

Only silver_transactions needs replacing. The gold tables are rebuilt from it when the pipeline runs, so they will be correct once it is fixed. Output columns stay the same.

Two things I checked:
- Since ingest_ts is always the day after txn_ts, the current txn_date is wrong for all rows, which matches the 4600 alert count. The raw rows have no late arrivals.
- Does the fix change the row set? No, the WHERE filter is unchanged.

One residual risk is that the intended date is something other than the txn_ts date, such as a business-day cutoff. Nothing in the evidence suggests that.

{"diagnosis": "silver_transactions derives txn_date from ingest_ts (the batch delivery time, one day after the transaction) instead of txn_ts, since the DE-398 refactor; all 4600 POSTED rows are off by one day, and the gold tables inherit the wrong dates.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.93, "pre_sql": [], "step_overrides": {"silver_transactions": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS txn_ts, CAST(txn_ts AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM raw_transactions WHERE status = 'POSTED'"}}
